newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Maseca results seen hit by subsidy issue.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Maseca results seen hit by subsidy issue.

text.p: Mexican corn-flour giant Grupo Industrial Maseca SA may not produce the stellar results that shareholders are used to when first-quarter earnings are released later this month, analysts said.
Maseca took a blow in March when the government said it would not increase the ceiling on corn-flour subsidies, just when seasonal demand for corn flour increases.
The move will likely prevent any real increases in sales or profits for the quarter, but should not cause a big dropoff in profitability because it did not affect January or February, analysts said.

The table shows an average of Q1 1997 results predicted by four analysts surveyed by Reuters. To account for the impact of inflation, Q1 1996 results are adjusted upwards by March-on-March inflation of 24.45 percent.
Net profit 144 million pesos 150.7 million pesos
Operating income 208 million pesos 212.5 million pesos
Gross profit 356 million pesos 353 million pesos
Gross profit per tonne 650 pesos 760 pesos
Analysts said the subsidies are part of a government program to control the price of tortillas, a staple of the Mexican diet traditionally made from fresh corn or corn flour.

Stock prices for Maseca, which controls about 70 percent of the domestic corn-flour market, slipped on the news as investors feared Maseca would be forced to sell more non-subsidized corn flour to tortilla producers.
"It's obviously going to hurt," Scott Weiss, an analyst with D.A. Campbell in Los Angeles, told Reuters. "No matter how much demand goes up, volumes are still going to be flat."
Another analyst who asked not to be named said March sales volumes would "come to a screeching halt, maybe even contract two or three percent."
"Plus the fact that corn prices have gone down so much (over the past year) will make revenues look small," Kevin Kirkeby, an analyst with Robert Fleming in New York, told Reuters.
Compounding the subsdidy ceiling problem for Maseca is a new Mexican government system of determining corn prices, called the Indifference Price of corn, used in calculating subsidies.
